payload.title: Poke-in operations: pause, resume, set rung, wake now, redirect, undo
payload.description:
Each is one operation in the operation table, so the newsroom and the CLI have the same names: `agents pause` and `resume` (one agent or the whole site, with a reason), `agents set-rung` (admin, with a reason and optional scope), `agents wake` (run now for a subject), `agents redirect` (give an instruction for a subject; it reaches the next run as steering), and `agents undo --run` (reverses what one run wrote, using the versions and decisions it recorded; anything that cannot be undone, such as a sent email, is listed and not attempted). Each is recorded with who and why.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Every poke-in works the same in the newsroom and the CLI.
- Undo restores the records a run changed and lists what it cannot reverse.
- A pause takes effect before the next run starts.
- Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs (below).

**Gherkin features needed**
- poke-in.feature: pausing stops the next run; set-rung needs an admin; wake now runs once; a redirect appears in the next run's input; undo restores the previous version and names what was already sent.

**Infrastructure as code touched:** None.

**Part of:** Human surface: Today, poke-in operations and explanations. Slice code H3 in `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md` (section 12).
**Standing rules:** no fallbacks, no workarounds, no interim systems, no arbitrary caps; no text in DynamoDB; indexes over scans; no AppSync subscriptions; nothing created by hand in AWS; no real email addresses in specs or fixtures; status shown as words and marks, never colour alone.
